_comment: globalConcurrencyLimit bounds children WITHIN one batch. It does NOT bound how wide a `runs.all` fan-out may open, which upstream also states in its own docs; keep a fan-out inside the provider's concurrency budget in the `concurrency` map of config/routing.json yourself. `parallel.maxTasks` and `parallel.concurrency` are dormant as of pi-subagents 0.57.0 — their resolvers are never called — and are kept set so a later release finds a conservative value already here. A run also carries a cumulative child budget, maxSubagentSpawnsPerRun, default 64 and live unset. See docs/adr/0005-unbounded-fan-out-on-runs-all.md. || Two spawn budgets are set here, 20 each. maxSubagentSpawnsPerRun 20 is BELOW the package default of 64 and is CUMULATIVE over one run tree with claims never released or refunded (pi-subagents docs/configuration.md:262), so it is a total-spawn budget, not a width cap: a long multi-wave research run can exhaust it part-way through and be refused its next child. Size it against the widest workflow you actually run before lowering it further. maxActiveAsyncRunsPerSession 20 replaces UNLIMITED, not a default of 4 - unset or 0 keeps unlimited behaviour (docs/configuration.md:272); it bounds concurrently active top-level async runs and does NOT bound runs.all fan-out, since workflow children do not reserve a slot. || maxSubagentSpawnsPerSession is deliberately NOT set, and the omission is a decision (2026-08-27) rather than an oversight. The rule applied was: cap it if it bounds simultaneity, leave it unlimited if it is a session total. It is a session total - it counts every child launched in one parent session including the completed and the failed ones (pi-subagents docs/configuration.md:252), and its counter has no release path - so setting it would cap how much work one session may do in total, not how much it does at once. maxActiveAsyncRunsPerSession above is the concurrency-shaped key and is already 20. Do not add the session key expecting it to bound width. || asyncWidget is false, and it is a BUG FIX rather than a preference. The key hides the package's own above-editor block for active background runs (pi-subagents docs/configuration.md 'asyncWidget'; read at src/extension/index.ts:415 -> widgetEnabled :521). With it on there are TWO aboveEditor widgets, and their vertical order is unstable: the host keeps same-placement widgets in a Map and renders them in insertion order (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/modes/interactive/interactive-mode.js:285 and :1723-1725), but setExtensionWidget deletes the key and re-inserts it on EVERY update, content-only changes included (:1629-1633 then :1657). Re-insertion moves a key to the tail, so the rendered order is least-recently-painted-first and the block that painted most recently sinks to the bottom. Two painters on unsynchronised timers therefore TRADE PLACES rather than tie-break, and at a sub-second repaint rate the two blocks visibly swap several times a second. Only being the single aboveEditor painter fixes that; height-locking one of the two cannot. A second, independent cause is height: the package's block builds from lines each conditional on a field being present (src/tui/render.ts:1278-1288) and locks its row count only in the progressive and single-line tiers, never in the full tier a normal-height terminal picks (:1581-1584), while repainting on the child's own write rate (25ms debounce, src/tui/async-job-tracker.ts:47 and :467) rather than on a display cadence. What this does NOT disable, deliberately: fleetView stays true at its default belowEditor placement, so the Fleet inspector (Ctrl+Alt+F), /subagents-fleet, completion notifications and lifecycle events are all untouched. The replacement panel is extensions/dispatch/fleet-widget.ts, which truncates by display width and honours the host's MAX_WIDGET_LINES of 10 (interactive-mode.js:1702). Setting this back to true means accepting the swap again. || toolDescriptionMode is 'custom', which makes pi-subagents read the model-facing description of the `subagent` tool from config/subagent-tool-description.md instead of using its own (src/extension/tool-description.ts). The shipped default describes the PACKAGE's example roster - its worked example routes to agent:'reviewer', which is not one of the roles in agents/ - and its promptGuidelines require an { action: 'list' } round trip before every execution. Three consequences, all intended. The lookup is <cwd>/.pi/subagent-tool-description.md first and then getAgentDir()/subagent-tool-description.md, which is where install.sh's `link_one required config/subagent-tool-description.md` puts the tracked file; the agent-dir ROOT, not the nested extensions/subagent/ directory this config file goes to. SUBAGENT_SAFETY_GUIDANCE is re-appended whatever the custom file says, so prose cannot remove the runtime guardrails and a pasted copy of them is dead weight. And setting the key to ANY value makes buildSubagentToolPromptMetadata() return an empty object, so the tool contributes no promptSnippet and no promptGuidelines - which costs nothing here, because a custom SYSTEM.md already suppresses PI's whole `Guidelines:` section, and is the reason the workflowScript call protocol lives in the tool description and nowhere else. FAIL MODE: a missing, empty, unreadable or over-50-KB file does not fall back to the short default description, it falls back to the 6 KB FULL one behind a single console.warn - hence the `required` install row. Fork editing this: the roles, the model example and the width number in that file are yours, not upstream's. Restart pi after changing either the mode or the file.
